title: I Am More
abstract:
Abstract

This short documentary shares the story of two housemaids (Hawa Zawadi & Gloria Cortez), in the Middle East who, in an attempt to have a better future, use their free time wisely to practice their hobbies. The documentary covers a series of topics including Zawadi and Cortez’s personal backgrounds, the struggles they face on a daily basis and most importantly, their hobbies outside their working space. They explain the philosophy behind taking such drastic measures to ensure the livelihood to a better future and reveal that working as a housemaid is not an obstacle, but rather a challenge that pushes them to their limitations to fight for their future. They discuss the significance of their hobbies and how they always manage to put some time aside for fun and skill development to draw the right path to their dreams. Finally, they express their emotions about how not letting go of their goals under hard conditions, makes them feel stronger and hopeful whenever they feel that life is falling apart.

Artist Statement

My short documentary offers a unique insight into a much-debated social issue that is prevalent in the Middle East; the issue of housemaids. Through a series of interviews with two housemaids currently working in the Middle East, my documentary looks to showcase the true significance of this often overlooked job. Therefore, by looking at two happy souls, who must resort to creative means to help them endure the hardships that come along with the life of a housemaid in the Middle East, this film seeks to achieve two goals. One, it attempts to empower housemaids all over the Middle East by giving them an opportunity to freely express themselves through sharing different hobbies that they do other than work. Two, this documentary also serves a piece of advice to all women, in that tells them that limitations are just constraints that people create to not only make themselves feel superior, but to also make others feel inferior.
